study_identification_part.si4_title: Individual-level deviations from normative brain morphology in violence, psychosis, and psychopathy

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: To assess individual patterns of deviations from normative brain morphology in persons with a history of severe violence and schizophrenia spectrum disorder (SSD-V), compared to persons with schizophrenia spectrum disorder without violence (SSD-NV), persons with violence without schizophrenia (nonSSD-V), and healthy controls (HC), using normative modeling to investigate heterogeneous brain morphometric deviations associated with violence and psychosis.

caa6_deviation_metric.answer: Z-scores; extreme deviations defined as |Z| > 2 (Z > 2 for positive deviations, Z < -2 for negative deviations); percentage of individuals with extreme deviations per ROI; total outlier count per individual
caa6_deviation_metric.reason: The paper explicitly describes the use of Z-scores to quantify deviations, with extreme deviations defined as absolute Z > 2. Multiple summary metrics were calculated including percentage of subjects with extreme deviations per ROI and count of extreme deviations per individual.
caa6_deviation_metric.supporting_text: To summarize inter-individual variation within each group (SSD-V, SSD-NV, nonSSD-V and HC), we computed deviation scores (Z-scores) by separating them into positive and negative deviations. The percentage of subjects within each group with extreme positive (Z > 2) and negative (Z < -2) deviations at a given ROI were compared and reported [20]. Further, we examined which ROIs consistently exhibited extreme deviations in each modality (cortical area and thickness, subcortical volume) by quantifying the percentage of extreme deviations observed in each ROI for each diagnostic group. Then, we quantified the number of extreme deviations per individual to compare if participants from all diagnostic groups had a higher count of extreme deviations in general as compared to healthy controls.

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa7_association_analysis: Group comparisons of deviation scores using general linear models (GLM) via PALM toolkit with permutation testing, controlling for age and demeaning data/independent variables; ICV included as covariate for volume/area analyses; 1:1 age and scanner matching between HC and diagnostic groups using logistic regression distance (matchIt package); family-wise error correction for multiple comparisons (ROIs, modalities, contrasts); Cohen's d effect sizes computed. Permutation tests for group differences in frequency of extreme deviations (positive vs negative). Associations between PCL-R psychopathy scores and deviation scores tested using GLM in PALM with 10,000 permutations, controlling for age, psychosis status, and ICV (for area/volume).
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: Heterogeneous patterns of individual brain deviations were observed in violence and psychosis, with SSD-V showing most prominent extreme negative deviations in collateral transverse sulcus, lingual gyrus, and cerebellum, differing from SSD-NV (parieto-occipital and suborbital sulci) and nonSSD-V (paracentral and middle frontal regions); no significant associations with psychopathy traits were found.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa9_key_findings_detailed: The study found overall heterogeneous patterns of individual brain morphological deviations associated with violence and psychosis. SSD-V showed extreme negative deviations in 2.6% of cortical area regions, 1.18% of cortical thickness regions, and 2.1% of subcortical regions, compared to 1.5%, 0.95%, and 0.6% respectively in HC. The regions most affected in SSD-V included the left anterior (13.2%) and right posterior (10.5%) collateral transverse sulcus area, the left medial lingual gyrus area (10.5%), and right cerebellar cortex volume (10.5%). SSD-V differed significantly from HC in the right subcallosal area (p_mc-fwe=0.020, t=4.5, d=1.17) and left medial occipito-temporal and lingual sulcus thickness (p_c-fwe=0.022, t=4.3, d=0.99). SSD-NV showed most extreme deviations in the right parieto-occipital and suborbital sulcus areas (7.2% each), significantly larger positive deviations in left inferior lateral ventricle volume (p_c-fwe=0.0085, t=4.2, d=0.61) and pallidum volume (p_c-fwe=0.025, t=4.0, d=0.57) compared to HC. NonSSD-V showed highest extreme negative deviations in the left paracentral lobule/sulcus (20%) and middle frontal gyrus (15%). Approximately 89.5% of SSD-V and 65% of nonSSD-V had at least one extreme deviation from the normative range. No significant associations were found between PCL-R psychopathy scores and brain morphology deviations after multiple comparison correction, though trend-level positive associations were observed in the right subparietal sulcus area (d=1.8, p_unc=0.0041) and parieto-inferior supramarginal gyral thickness (d=1.8, p_unc=0.0056).

caa10_key_limitations.answer: Relatively small sample sizes especially for violence groups; male-only sample limiting generalizability; ROI-level analysis may have lower sensitivity than vertex-wise approaches; no control for substance use effects; antipsychotic medication effects not controlled; most severely ill/aggressive individuals excluded due to consent/safety concerns; violence defined as binary lifetime variable; cross-sectional design unable to distinguish disease mechanisms from developmental trajectories
caa10_key_limitations.supporting_text: The study has some limitations. The relatively small number of subjects with a history of violence, as well as the male only sample (which reflects the predominance of men in the study group of interest), might limit the generalizability of the current study. ... Although the Freesurfer Destrieux atlas comprises 148 cortical ROIs, atlas defined cortical parcellations have shown lower representations of true associations and prediction accuracy than vertex-wise analyses [67]. Moreover, the models were not corrected for substance use which could affect brain morphological characteristics ... Further, we did not control for cumulative effects of antipsychotic medication which may also affect brain morphology but are also overlapping with clinical groups and their associated psychopathological characteristics. The most severely ill or aggressive persons in the forensic psychiatry wards or prisons were not eligible for participation due to lack of ability to consent or/and safety concerns. Violence was defined as a lifetime binary variable which was narrower than the WHO definition. ... Finally, an inherent limitation in all cross-sectional neuroimaging studies is the inability to distinguish between specific disease mechanisms and the effects of early-life influences and developmental trajectories.

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa11_application_notes: The study represents one of the first applications of normative modeling to forensic psychiatry populations. Age- and scanner-matched controls (1:1 ratio) were used for group comparisons. Multiple correction levels were reported (uncorrected, FDR for ROIs, FDR for ROIs+contrasts, FDR for ROIs+contrasts+modalities) to provide transparency about statistical stringency. The study utilized publicly available pretrained braincharts normative models to ensure reproducibility and facilitate future replication studies. Separate analyses were conducted for positive and negative deviations to capture bidirectional abnormalities.

general_note_part.gn1_general_notes: The calibration set of 998 healthy controls (390 male/608 female) included both males and females and was used to fine-tune the normative model parameters for application to the local scanners, but the actual clinical comparison group (HC, n=196) consisted only of males matched by age and scanner to the clinical groups. The normative model reference cohort was the large pretrained braincharts dataset (N=58,835 from 82 sites, ages 2-100 years). The study included comprehensive demographic characterization with PANSS, WASI-IQ, PCL-R, AUDIT, and DUDIT assessments. Two GE 3T scanners were used with slightly different sequences (FSPGR vs BRAVO). The Destrieux atlas provides 148 cortical ROIs per hemisphere. Violence was defined as court or hospital record verified episodes of homicide, attempted homicide, or physical/sexual violence toward others.
